messages:
incidentbot: PagerDuty PD-9471 fired \u2014 hosted-runtime /v1/generate 5xx rate >2.5% over 120s in us-west-2. Paging eng-oncall. https://pagerduty.local/PD-9471

alice: ack. i'm on call. i'll grab dashboards and check SRE alerts. on mobile for a few minutes. :iphone:

bob: i'm looking at proxy logs already. seeing a short spike of grpc 503/504 from proxy-usw-04. looks correlated with lots of tiny requests (~1-10 tokens) from a single customer blob.

carol: SLOs look okay overall. p99 latency unchanged, error bump is narrow (roughly 90-150s). no publicly reported errors in support channels yet.

bob: grabbing runtime logs for hosts in the affected AZ. quick snippet:
```
2026-03-15T21:03:12Z WARN runtime kv_prefill slow key=ctx:xyz took=942ms host=runtime-usw-03
2026-03-15T21:03:12Z ERROR runtime request 5xx model-serving: upstream timeout host=runtime-usw-03
2026-03-15T21:03:13Z ERROR proxy upstream reset id=3344 code=GRPC_UNAVAILABLE host=proxy-usw-04
```

bob: cluster autoscaler also did a brief scale-up at 21:02 then scaled down at 21:04. smells like cache warmup thrash causing transient KV prefill slowdowns and timeouts on a subset of workers. no OOMs in the logs.

alice: can someone grep for "kv_prefill" p99 in the last 15m and check autoscaler events? if this is only in one AZ we might be safe.

carol: running queries now. kv_prefill_p99 spiked to ~1.1s for ~2m on runtime-usw-03 and runtime-usw-04. miss rate up too. autoscaler events show 2 extra pods spun up at 21:02 and torn down at 21:04.

erin: i'm scanning support and Sentry. a handful of transient 5xx traces tied to the same RPC path, all short lived. no incoming support tickets attributable to user-facing failures.

incidentbot: PagerDuty note: PD-9471 auto-resolved after 3m 12s; condition cleared.

bob: errors returned to baseline as kv_prefill p99 fell back below threshold and the transient routing imbalance cleared after autoscale finished.

alice: conclusion: transient kv prefill latency during autoscale + bursty small-batch traffic caused short-lived upstream timeouts. no customer impact observed.

alice: proposed follow-ups (assigned):
- bob: open an alert-tuning PR to reduce noise and add a guard based on kv_prefill_p99 so autoscale-induced warmup doesn't trigger PD as easily. include graphs and rollback plan.
- carol: update runtime runbook to include kv_prefill checks and autoscaler event lookup commands.
- erin: draft a one-paragraph support template in case customers ask.

carol: runbook snippet to add:
```
# check for proxy GRPC errors
kubectl logs -l app=proxy -n hosted --since=10m | grep GRPC_UNAVAILABLE || true
# kv prefill latency p99
kubectl logs -l app=runtime -n hosted --since=10m | grep kv_prefill | sed -n '1,200p'
# recent autoscaler events
kubectl get events -n hosted --field-selector involvedObject.kind=HorizontalPodAutoscaler --since=15m
```

bob: i'll also add a grafana panel correlating kv_prefill_p99, proxy_503_rate, and autoscaler_activity so future triage is faster.

alice: agree we should also consider a temporary alert suppression rule for autoscale=true bursts (low risk) but only after a short review. do not change production behavior without PR and rollback steps.

erin: drafting support template now and will drop it into the post-incident doc.

alice: handoff: bob(alert PR + grafana), carol(runbook), erin(support template). i'll follow up in the morning to confirm no recurrence.

incidentbot: Thread closed by alice. Follow-ups set: bob(alert PR), carol(runbook), erin(support template).
